name: Pedigree Editor Module
description: This module will allow the use of a pedigree editor to build a pedigree diagram, saving the diagram into a field with the tag @PEDIGREE_EDITOR

system-settings.name:
The '@PEDIGREE' action tag marks a notes field as a pedigree diagram, using the project (or system) configured default coding systems - see 'Default Terminology' below.
The default 'Hide Text' flag can be overriden in the action tag by appending
  • =HIDE_TEXT - Hide the text area.
  • =SHOW_TEXT - Show the text area.
An action tag of @PEDIGREE=HIDE_TEXT will hide the text area for the field.

The Hide Text flag indicates if the text area containing the FHIR representation of the diagram should be hidden.
The default 'Hide Text' flag can be overriden in the action tag by appending
  • =HIDE_TEXT - Hide the text area.
  • =SHOW_TEXT - Show the text area.
An action tag of @PEDIGREE=HIDE_TEXT will hide the text area for the field.

The original version of this plugin used a custom FHIR format, in version 0.3 this was changed to a format defined by GA4GH. The format field allows the format to be selected, fhir_v1 is the old format, while GA4GH is the new format. If GA4GH is selected it will still read the old format. The new format is recommended and has better round tripping. In version 0.4 five new formats were added, PED, PEDX, DADA2, DADA2X and internal. PED is a very simple format that only captures the base structure of the pedigree, but could be used to default the value of the field based on other fields in the instrument. PEDX is an extension to this that wraps the PED format in an XML document to allow the resulting SVG image produced to also be stored. DADA2 and DADA2X are a customization of the PED format for use at DADA2.org. It includes an extra field for life status. Finally internal uses the openpedigree internal json model which is not documented and may not be compatible with future versions of the external module but should allow the best round tripping. This format and PED do not include a svg version of the pedigree diagram so will not show the diagram except when the diagram is saved into the system.

choices.name: PEDX - XML format PED and possible SVG Image
DADA2X - XML format DADA2 and possible SVG Image
Open-pedigree internal format - may break with new version of EM

system-settings.name:
A complicated pedigree may be large, the compress data setting indicates if the data should be compressed.
The default 'Compress Data' value can be overridden in the action tag by appending
  • =NEVER_COMPRESS - Never Compress.
  • =COMPRESS_LARGE - Compress Large Diagrams >65K.
  • =ALWAYS_COMPRESS - Always Compress
An action tag of @PEDIGREE=ALWAYS_COMPRESS will always compress the data in the field.
The Ontology Server URL setting indicates the server to use to lookup disorders and phenotypes, leaving blank will result in the default value of 'https://tx.ontoserver.csiro.au/fhir'
Maximum number of seconds to wait for the Ontology Server before giving up. Leave blank to use the default of 10 seconds.
The fhir server may require some form of authentication, currently only OAuth2 Client Credentials is supported. Communication with the FHIR server is made by the redcap server, not the users browser.
FHIR valuesets to use for disorders, phenotypes and genes to use for @PEDIGREE tag.

Custom terminology requires a code system, valueset and valid code regular expression to be defined for disorders, phenotypes and genes.
A regular expression of '.+' should be used if the code systems values are not regular.
The following values are used for HPO and SCT tags:
EntryCode SystemValuesetRegex
OMIM (HPO Disorder)http://www.omim.orghttp://www.omim.org/vs[0-9]+
HPO (HPO Phenotype)http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/hp.owlhttp://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/hp.owl?vs^(http:\/\/)|(HP:)
Genehttp://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/HGNC/hgnc.owlhttp://www.genenames.org[0-9]+
SnomedCT (SCT Disorder)http://snomed.info/scthttp://snomed.info/sct?fhir_vs=refset/32570581000036105[0-9]+
SnomedCT (SCT Phenotype)http://snomed.info/scthttp://ga4gh.org/fhir/ValueSet/phenotype[0-9]+

Configuring a repeating instrument here lets a pedigree node be linked to a row of that instrument and have its @PEDIGREE_FIELD-tagged answers imported (read-only, one-time snapshot) into the node's form. See the module README for the @PEDIGREE_FIELD action tag syntax.
Repeating instrument to search/import from when linking a pedigree node
Field used to search/display a row when linking a pedigree node (add one or more, e.g. first/last name)

Controls how the pedigree node-edit form is built for this project.
  • Tags only - the form is built entirely from @PEDIGREE_FIELD-tagged fields on the configured repeating instrument. No disorders/genes/phenotypes legend unless you tag fields for it.
  • Default + tags - starts from open-pedigree's built-in default form (name, gender, disorders/genes/phenotypes legend, etc., entered directly in the editor) and adds any @PEDIGREE_FIELD-tagged fields as one extra tab.
  • Advanced - you supply your own FHIR Questionnaire below. @PEDIGREE_FIELD tags are not scanned at all; link an item to a REDCap field by hand-authoring a 'questionnaire-redcap-source' extension on it (see the module README for examples).

choices.name: Tags only - build the form entirely from @PEDIGREE_FIELD-tagged fields
Default + tags - built-in form, plus a tab for @PEDIGREE_FIELD-tagged fields
Advanced - I will supply my own FHIR Questionnaire

project-settings.name: Advanced: FHIR Questionnaire JSON (used verbatim; see README for examples and the 'questionnaire-redcap-source' linking pattern)
